note: National programmes (v3, sim-endgame): the late-game goals of the state. Each level is a real programme (historical levels carry history's date in "hist"; the ghost of history launches them then) or a real proposal that history did not carry out ("hist": null, with a named advocate and a verbatim cite). A level is paid from the treasury in quarterly instalments (cost x the era's gold scale x difficulty) and, once complete, sets lasting terms ("effects", stream types as in FORKS.md, from completion to the end of the game) and a track gain ("legacy", % of a score track, growing to full over four years). Historical levels open up to 8 years before history at +4% cost per year early. "expand" is a repeatable scale-up (a gold sink for late surpluses, like Civ VI district projects): expansions open after level 1; each costs as much again as the first (x2, x3, ...) and gives 20% less. Costs, turns, effects and legacy sizes are gameplay balance, not historical claims.

programmes.name: MASHAV: international development cooperation
programmes.desc: Israel's agency for international development cooperation sends agronomists, doctors and trainers abroad and trains students from Africa, Asia and Latin America in Israel.

levels.name: Found MASHAV
levels.desc: Golda Meir's agency for cooperation with newly independent states, above all in Africa.

cite.quote: MASHAV, Israel’s Agency for International Development Cooperation at Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, was established in 1958 following the vision of then Foreign Minister Golda Meir and Prime Minister David Ben Gurion

expand.name: Training centres and missions abroad
expand.desc: More courses in Israel and longer missions abroad: friends in the UN and in the capitals.

programmes.name: Talpiot: the army's science and technology programme
programmes.desc: An elite IDF programme that trains a few dozen recruits a year in physics, mathematics and computing for the defence research establishment; many graduates later found technology firms.

levels.name: Found Talpiot
levels.desc: Chief of Staff Rafael Eitan approves the programme after the lessons of the Yom Kippur War.

cite.quote: In 1979, Eitan took that leap and green-lighted Talpiot, although initially he gave it one year.

expand.name: More Talpiot classes and defence research units
expand.desc: Larger cohorts and research units: more scientists for the army and, later, for industry.

programmes.name: The start-up economy
programmes.desc: The state seeds high technology: research grants under the 1984 R&D law, incubators for new firms and the Yozma venture-capital funds.

levels.name: The R&D law: the Chief Scientist's grants
levels.desc: The Law for the Encouragement of Industrial Research and Development funds a share of firms' research through the Chief Scientist.

cite.quote: Pursuant to the Encouragement of Industrial Research and Development Law, 1984 and the regulations promulgated thereunder

levels.name: Technological incubators
levels.desc: Government-backed incubators give new firms, many founded by engineers from the former Soviet Union, two years of funding and premises.

cite.quote: it was Erlich who established the government incubator program

levels.name: Yozma: venture capital
levels.desc: A government fund matches private and foreign venture capital in ten new funds.

cite.quote: The 40% public share was conditional on attracting at least 60% private capital and a reputable foreign financial partner
The activity that Erlich initiated at the end of 1992 while serving as Chief Scientist at the Industry and Trade Ministry gave birth to ten entrepreneurial funds.

expand.name: Expand research and development grants
expand.desc: Larger grants and more incubators beyond the centre of the country.

programmes.name: Space and cyber
programmes.desc: A national space agency for satellites, then a national cyber bureau and a cyber-security authority that defend the networks the economy now runs on.

levels.name: The Israel Space Agency
levels.desc: A national agency coordinates civilian and defence space research.

cite.quote: The Israel Space Agency, founded following a government decision in 1983, is a national agency operating under the auspices of the Ministry of Science and Technology.

levels.name: The National Cyber Bureau
levels.desc: Government Resolution 3611 sets a national cyber strategy and a bureau in the Prime Minister's Office to carry it out.

cite.quote: The current National cyber-strategy of Israel stemmed from the National Cyber Initiative and was declared in the Government Resolution 3611 ‘Advancing the national capacity in cyberspace’.
The Israel National Cyber Bureau (INCB) was established to develop and implement the strategy.

levels.name: The National Cyber Security Authority
levels.desc: An operational authority that defends civilian networks and critical infrastructure.

cite.quote: Driven by the 2011 strategy, the government resolved to establish a National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) in February 2015

expand.name: Cyber and space research
expand.desc: More satellites, cyber units and research chairs.

programmes.name: The missile shield
programmes.desc: A layered defence against rockets and missiles: Arrow against ballistic missiles, Iron Dome against short-range rockets, David's Sling in between and the Iron Beam laser.

levels.name: Arrow batteries deployed
levels.desc: The Arrow interceptor, built with the United States, guards against ballistic missiles.

cite.quote: The system became operational in 2000 in Israel

levels.name: Iron Dome over the towns
levels.desc: Iron Dome batteries around the towns in range of rockets.

cite.quote: Israel’s Iron Dome missile defense system for the first time intercepted rockets fired from Gaza.

levels.name: David's Sling
levels.desc: The middle layer, against heavy rockets, drones and cruise missiles.

cite.quote: The David’s Sling missile defense system, which is designed to stop medium-range rockets, drones and cruise missiles, became operational in Israel.

levels.name: Iron Beam
levels.desc: A high-energy laser that intercepts rockets and drones at a small cost per shot.

cite.quote: Israel will introduce Biden to its still-developing “Iron Beam” system, which in testing has shown that it will likely be able to down missiles with laser beams

levels.advocate: Rafael and the Defence Ministry (still in development, July 2022)

expand.name: More batteries and interceptor stocks
expand.desc: Deeper magazines and more batteries: fewer strikes get through.

programmes.name: Water independence: desalination
programmes.desc: Large seawater desalination plants on the coast, built and run by private firms under state tenders, end the country's dependence on rain and the Kinneret.

levels.name: Large desalination plants
levels.desc: The government approves large reverse-osmosis plants on the coast (Ashkelon, Palmachim, Hadera).

cite.quote: The Israeli government approved their construction as far back as 2002

levels.name: Desalination for most of the drinking water
levels.desc: Sorek and Ashdod join the coastal plants; six plants supply most of the drinking water.

cite.quote: Israel was isolated from the full scale of the catastrophe thanks to six desalination plants that provide 70 percent of its drinking water.

levels.name: 750 million m3 a year: the government's 2020 target
levels.desc: History's plants fell short of the capacity the government had set for 2020; building it in full adds a reserve for drought years.

cite.quote: According to a government decision, by 2020 the desalination plants should reach a capacity of 750 million cubic meters.

levels.advocate: The government of Israel (decision on 750 million m3 of desalination capacity by 2020)

levels.name: Water for Jordan, solar power for Israel
levels.desc: The water-for-energy deal signed by Israel, Jordan and the United Arab Emirates in November 2021, which history did not carry out.

cite.quote: Jordan would export about 600 megawatts of electricity generated from solar energy, while Israel would evaluate the export of up to 200 million cubic meters of desalinated water to Jordan

levels.advocate: The governments of Israel, Jordan and the UAE (memorandum signed in Dubai, November 2021)

expand.name: More desalination capacity
expand.desc: Another plant on the coast and pipes to refill the Kinneret.

programmes.name: The gas fields
programmes.desc: Offshore natural gas from the Tamar and Leviathan fields replaces imported coal and oil in the power stations and is exported to Egypt and Jordan.

levels.name: Tamar comes ashore
levels.desc: Gas from the Tamar field reaches Israel's power stations.

cite.quote: Natural gas from Tamar field reaches Israel

levels.name: The sovereign wealth fund
levels.desc: A law puts a share of the state's gas revenues into a fund invested abroad, as the Sheshinski committee proposed.

cite.quote: The law establishing the sovereign wealth fund was enacted in 2014.

levels.name: Leviathan and exports to Egypt
levels.desc: The larger Leviathan field starts production; gas flows to Egypt and Jordan under long-term contracts.

cite.quote: Natural gas from Leviathan started to flow to the Israeli domestic market in December 2019.
Egypt started importing natural gas from Israel ‘s largest offshore gas field Leviathan on Wednesday

levels.name: The EastMed pipeline to Europe
levels.desc: The pipeline to Greece and Italy agreed in January 2020 and never built: gas exports to Europe and a closer alliance with Greece and Cyprus.

cite.quote: The governments of Greece , Israel and Cyprus have signed an agreement to build a pipeline that could supply Europe with 4 percent of its annual gas needs by the middle of the decade.

levels.advocate: The governments of Greece, Israel and Cyprus (agreement signed in Athens, 2 January 2020)

expand.name: Develop further fields
expand.desc: Licences for the smaller fields and a gas grid to industry.

programmes.name: Peace dividends
programmes.desc: Agreements between governments turned into trade: industrial zones whose goods enter the United States duty-free, and the investment and tourism that followed normalisation.

levels.name: Qualifying Industrial Zones with Jordan
levels.desc: Goods made jointly in Jordan and Israel enter the United States duty-free.

cite.quote: In 1996, Congress authorized the creation of Qualifying Industrial Zones (QIZs), thereby entitling goods jointly produced by Israel and either Jordan or Egypt to enter the United States duty free.

levels.name: Qualifying Industrial Zones with Egypt
levels.desc: The same arrangement with Egypt: the largest trade link since the peace treaty.

cite.quote: Finally, in December of 2004, following an agreement between Israel and Egypt, the USTR designated the first three QIZs in Egypt

levels.name: Abraham Accords trade and investment
levels.desc: Flights, investment funds and trade with the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Morocco.

cite.quote: Abraham Accords Peace Agreement: Treaty of Peace, Diplomatic Relations and Full Normalization Between the United Arab Emirates and the State of Israel

expand.name: Regional trade and tourism deals
expand.desc: More routes, joint ventures and visitors with the states at peace with Israel.

programmes.name: Development plans for Arab localities
programmes.desc: Five-year government plans for Arab towns: transport, education, employment, housing, local budgets and, from 2021, policing.

levels.name: Resolution 922: the first five-year plan
levels.desc: A five-year plan of about NIS 10 billion to narrow the gaps between Arab and Jewish localities.

cite.quote: A similar push to end persistent gaps between Arab and Jewish Israelis in 2015, known as 922, allocated around NIS 10 billion — and only 62 percent was ultimately spent, according to official statistics.

levels.name: The 2021 plans for Arab communities
levels.desc: Two plans of over NIS 32 billion for the economy of Arab communities and against crime.

cite.quote: The cabinet passed two wide-ranging plans on Sunday that would allocate over NIS 32 billion ($10 billion) for Arab communities

expand.name: Spend the plans in full
expand.desc: History spent only part of the money: schools, roads, planning and policing in Arab towns beyond the plans' budgets.

programmes.name: Universal health care
programmes.desc: The National Health Insurance Law makes membership of a health fund universal, financed by a health tax.

levels.name: National Health Insurance
levels.desc: Every resident is insured with a health fund of their choice.

cite.quote: In June 1994, the Israeli parliament passed the National Health Insurance Law (NHIL), a turning point in the history of the Israeli healthcare system.
Under the State Health Insurance Law, effective from January 1, 1995, every Israeli resident

expand.name: Clinics and hospitals in the periphery
expand.desc: New hospitals and clinics in the Negev and the Galilee.
